title: Run competitor research for a small business in 30 minutes
summary: Paste three competitor URLs and any pricing or about-page text you copied. Get a short strengths/gaps snapshot and three opportunities — with no invented prices or features.

tests.prompt:
Run a 30-minute competitor snapshot for my small business. Use only the URLs and notes I provide — do not browse inventively or invent pricing.

My business: [ONE-LINE DESCRIPTION]
What I sell / who I serve: [NOTES]
Competitors:
1) [NAME] — [URL] — notes: [OPTIONAL]
2) [NAME] — [URL] — notes: [OPTIONAL]
3) [NAME] — [URL] — notes: [OPTIONAL]
Extra material I pasted: [PRICING PAGE TEXT / ABOUT TEXT / ADS COPY OR "none"]

For each competitor output:
- Positioning in one sentence
- 3 strengths (tied to evidence I provided)
- 3 weaknesses or gaps (hedge if evidence is thin)
- Pricing signals: only what appears in my paste; else "not in materials"
Then: 3 opportunities for my business, each with a why
Finally: open questions I should verify manually this week

Never invent features, customers, or prices.

setup.agent: Chat model with pasted page text (do not trust unverified browsing claims)
steps: Pick 3 competitors and open their site, pricing, and about pages.
Paste key sections into the prompt with your one-line description.
Run the prompt and highlight anything that needs a manual check.
Verify pricing and claims on the live sites before acting.
Turn one opportunity into a task for this week.
setup.approvalStep: Treat output as a hypothesis list. Confirm every price and feature on the source site.
failureModes: Generic SWOT language with no evidence
Comparing yourself to the wrong market segment

toolPicks.why: Quarterly reminder + sheet of competitor URLs.
Store snapshots over time in your own DB.

faq.q: How many competitors should I include?
faq.a: Three is enough for a half hour. Add more only if they are true alternatives.

faq.q: What if the model gets something wrong?
faq.a: Believe the live website over the draft. Fix your pasted source text and re-run.
